messages:
Mia Chen: quick heads-up — running workload X with Mistral-8x7B sliding-window + RoPE scaling and seeing ~18% tail latency regression vs baseline. KV cache churn looks suspicious. attached a tiny profile.

Omar Patel: can you paste the profile or flamegraph? which kernel selector was used? :thinking:

Mia Chen: flamegraph: https://perf.internal/runs/17645/fg.svg (short-lived) — kernel selector ended up choosing `fused_attention_fp16` for most steps, but at certain seq lengths it flipped to `generic_attention` which spikes time. also noticed KV pointer churn when window slides across padding boundaries.

Sasha Ivanov: hmm padding boundary — are we reusing prefix cache offsets or recomputing pos_ids? sliding-window should clamp pos ids, otherwise RoPE interp can misalign KV.

Dylan Park: paste of the sampling from the trace:
```
# simplified timeline
0-80: fused_attention_fp16 (good)
81-120: generic_attention (4x slower)
kv_ops: alloc/free spikes at 81, 121, 161
cache_hits drop from 98% -> 72%
```

Anjali Rao: what are the max_position_embeddings and the effective seq_len? 8x7B model default is 2048 but our sliding-window is 4096 virtualized, right?

Mia Chen: model max_pos=2048; we emulate longer context by sliding window and reusing KV segments. But when RoPE scaling is enabled, we scale positions >2048 which seems to change the kernel path.

Omar Patel: sounds like RoPE scaling values crossing a threshold which toggles an optimization path in the kernel selector. kernel selector checks `sequence_length` + `pos_embedding_mode` -> picks specialized kernels only when pos_ids monotonic and within base range. if we feed wrapped/scaled pos ids it falls back.

Sasha Ivanov: Another angle: head/kv dims for 8x7B are nonstandard (heads=16? head_dim changes after quant). The fused kernel has an alignment requirement (block of 64) — misaligned head dims force a slower codepath. check computed head_dim * num_heads vs expected alignment.

Dylan Park: repro command I ran locally:
```bash
# run sliding window profile
python bench.py --model mistral-8x7b --sliding-window 4096 --rope-scaling scaled --batch 4 --profile flame
```
profile output attached: 40% time in memory copy during KV rotate.

Anjali Rao: potential quick mitigations:
- clamp pos ids to [0, max_pos-1] and apply scaled RoPE in post-processing (avoid changing kernel path)
- force kernel selector to prefer fused_attention via a hint when head_dim aligns (unsafe but for experiments)
- adjust sliding-window logic to avoid crossing padding boundaries (pad to multiples of tile size)

Mia Chen: tried clamping pos ids — latency restores to within 3% of baseline but generated tokens after window boundary have slightly different logits (small distribution shift).

Omar Patel: that distribution drift could be due to RoPE phase discontinuity when you remap pos ids. For safety, we should add a deterministic continuity test in evals (prompt sets crossing window boundaries).

Sasha Ivanov: long-term fix ideas:
- support RoPE-relative updates in runtime so we can reuse KV without changing posids (store base offset in cache metadata)
- teach kernel selector about scaled RoPE so it keeps using fast kernel when mathematically equivalent
- for 8x7B, add an alignment shim: pad head_dim to next multiple for fused kernel only (transparent to model weights at runtime)

Dylan Park: FYI, quantization (int8) amplifies the problem — the slower path is even worse due to dequant reorder overhead. I hit a regression in per-token cost by ~25% in int8 runs.

perf-bot: automatic profiling note — peak GPU memory at failure window = 21.3 GB, average token latency 62.1ms, 95th = 142ms. See /runs/17645/details

Mia Chen: plan: 1) add a short exper script to clamp pos ids and run evals to measure generation drift (in progress). 2) add a kernel selector flag to force fused path for controlled runs. 3) add cache metadata prototype to carry `base_pos_offset`. Will open PRs for (2) and (3).

Omar Patel: +1. If you open PR for selector flag, mark it `perf-exper` and ensure it's opt-in. I'll help run dedicated cluster tests.

Anjali Rao: I'll create an eval job to run the sliding-window continuity tests across 10k prompts (edge cases: short prompts w/ a long continuation, exact tile boundary, and padded left contexts).

Sasha Ivanov: also add a quick kernel-level microbench for odd seq lengths (e.g., 81, 129, 193) to reproduce the path flip — that helped me once find an off-by-one in kernel eligibility.

Mia Chen: thanks all. filing a short incident ticket with action items and owner tags. I'll push the clamp experiment results later today. :thumbsup:
